 By Alex Jones, WSBTV.com and Michael Seiden, WSB-TV November 16, 2026 at 5:18 pm EST By Alex Jones, WSBTV.com and Michael Seiden, WSB-TV November 16, 2026 at 5:18 pm EST WALTON COUNTY, Ga. — Four children were among six people taken to hospitals Monday after a police chase involving a suspect wanted on outstanding felony warrants ended in a violent crash in Walton County.
 According to the Monroe Police Department, the pursuit began in Barrow County and involved 38-year-old Andrea Crane of Athens, who authorities said was wanted on outstanding felony warrants.
 Georgia State Patrol says Crane was driving a stolen Hyundai Elantra and crashed into a Nissan Altima and Chrysler Pacifica carrying the four injured children.
 [DOWNLOAD: Free WSB-TV News app for alerts as news breaks ] 
 GSP says a 4-year-old boy was airlifted to Children’s Healthcare of Atlanta. Police say he was in critical condition.
 A 9-year-old boy, a 7-year-old boy and a 2-year-old girl were taken to Children’s by ambulance.
 Two more adults, including Crane, were taken to Piedmont Walton Hospital.
 The extent of the other injuries is unknown.
 Andy Cason, an employee at Maxie Price Chevrolet in Monroe, said he was working when he heard sirens followed by several loud crashes.
 “It was definitely loud like a bomb went off,” Cason told Channel 2’s Michael Seiden .
 Cason grabbed his phone and photographed the chaotic aftermath outside the dealership.
 “We just heard a lot of sirens coming up and then we heard a lot of loud booms, like a car accident,” he said.

 Cason said he watched as a medical helicopter landed directly in front of the dealership to transport one of the injured children.
 “Then the next thing you know you see the life flight helicopter goes and lands right in front of the dealership. I see them load up the child. Hope the child is okay,” Cason said.
 The frightening scene immediately made him think about his own child.
 “The very first thing I did was call and check on him and make sure he was at school and everything was okay. Just a terrifying experience,” he said.
 Authorities said that after the collisions, a Barrow County deputy performed a PIT maneuver, ending the chase and taking Crane into custody.
 Authorities have not released details about the outstanding felony warrants or announced what additional charges Crane may face.
